subject: Subprocessor onboarding runbook: privacy controls, transfers, and SSQ
messages:
From: Anita Rao <anita.rao@medlogic.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: MedLogic Security <security@medlogic.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor SSQ and onboarding materials for MedLogic PII handling

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We're starting our formal security & privacy onboarding for Redwood as a subprocessor and I wanted to get the initial artifact request in writing so we can track dependencies on our side. High-level asks:

- Completed Security & Privacy Questionnaire (SSQ) covering PII classification, retention, export controls, and access controls (we attached our template).
- Annotated dataflow diagram that shows where PII is processed, which Redwood components touch vaults/keys, and what subprocessors (if any) are in the path.
- DPA exhibit: indicate whether you use SCCs / EU adequacy / specific transfer mechanisms; highlight any EU-hosted options and onshore-only carve-outs.
- KMS custody: who holds root keys, what proof of custody/attestations exist, and whether we can get a diagram of key flow for tokenization/redaction paths.
- Retention & deletion playbook for PII (customer-initiated deletion, backups, logs).

Timing: our security review is scheduled for 2025-10-21; would appreciate the completed SSQ and a first draft of the dataflow by 2025-10-14. We may need to request an evidence bundle (S3 / Drive link) before the review.

I've attached the MedLogic_SSQ_Initial.xlsx with the tabs we use. Please let me know if any of these items require an NDA or additional paperwork.

Best,
Anita Rao
Head of Security Operations
MedLogic Health

Attachment: MedLogic_SSQ_Initial.xlsx

Subject: Internal: MedLogic SSQ + dataflow — runbook and division of work

Team —

Forwarding Anita's SSQ request (below). MedLogic is explicit about PII handling and cross-border routing; they want the evidence bundle ready ahead of a 10/21 review. Please treat this as high priority. Specific asks: SSQ answers, annotated dataflow, DPA exhibit (transfer mechanism options), KMS custody diagram, and a retention/deletion playbook.

Please own the following:
- Marissa: SSQ answers (use MedLogic_SSQ_Initial.xlsx). Highlight tabs where we need legal/DPA exceptions (SCCs vs adequacy vs onshore-only). Also list current subprocessors and their regions; mark any that are EU-hosted.
- Jordan: Dataflow diagram draft (dataflow_v2.png) — annotate exactly which services touch PII, where KV cache is persisted, and the path for model telemetry. Indicate optional prefix caching and which subprocessors may receive kernel-level logs.
- Olga: KMS/Key custody notes and sample attestations; confirm whether customer-managed KMS is feasible for their plan and prepare a short paragraph for the DPA exhibit about key-splitting options.

Key points to emphasize in answers: least-privilege RBAC, tokenization and pseudonymization practices, access logging and retention windows, ability to provide exportable audit logs on request, and our fallback routing for capacity/region. If any of those aren't available in Hosted mode we should call that out and propose Dedicated/Private options.

Please reply in-thread with your attachments. I'm planning a 30-min call with Anita 10/9 at 10:00 PT to review the first draft.

Thanks — Camila

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Anita Rao <anita.rao@medlogic.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Oct 2025 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor SSQ and onboarding materials for MedLogic PII handling

Hi all — attaching the draft artifacts per Camila's runbook. Summary of answers and outstanding flags below; attachments: dataflow_v2.png, ssq_answers_v1.docx (answered inline in your template).

Summary highlights (short):
- PII classification: Redwood marks customer-provided text content as "sensitive PII" by default; we added mappings for common identifiers (SSN, health identifiers, DOB). See SSQ tab 'classification'.
- Access controls: RBAC enforced via scoped service accounts and token-level ACLs; privileged admin access is gated by SSO + JIT approval; audit logs retained 180 days by default (longer retention available as an add-on).
- Dataflow notes: dataflow_v2.png shows ingestion -> preprocessing -> runtime (model inference) -> KV cache (ephemeral) -> telemetry Kafka (redacted tokens) -> logs bucket. Subprocessors that touch telemetry/logs are listed in SSQ (StorageOps: US, LoggingVendor: EU).
- Transfers & DPA exhibit: Hosted customers default to Redwood-managed KMS and SCCs for EU transfers; we can propose an onshore-only carve-out by pinning resources to an EU region or enabling a Dedicated instance. We indicated SCCs in the DPA exhibit draft, and flagged one redline: MedLogic requests absolute onshore-only processing for a subset of PII fields — we'll need legal to sign off on the feasibility and cost.
- KMS custody: for Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) with HSM-backed attestations. For Hosted we provide KMS attestations and key lifecycle logs; Olga attached a short note.
- Retention & deletion: deletion requests are supported via API and we document backups retention and reversible windows. Logs retention and telemetry redaction are documented in the SSQ.

Outstanding items requiring action before 10/21 review:
1) Legal to confirm acceptability of MedLogic's proposed onshore-only carve-out and provide expected lead time and pricing (action: camila -> Legal).
2) Olga to provide the KMS attestation snippet and sample policy (action: olga).
3) Jordan to finalize the dataflow PNG with arrows labeled for subprocessor hops and KV lifetimes (action: jordan).

Drive evidence link (draft): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-evidence (I'll upload the full evidence pack after legal review).

Thanks — happy to walk through on the 10/9 call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Privacy Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: dataflow_v2.png; ssq_answers_v1.docx
